fixture.interpretation: Fixture mode replays one deliberately susceptible scripted reply sequence per task for every LLM arm (it follows planted instructions, uses a forged token, retries a timed-out write with a new key, acts on an ambiguous task). Those rows check the monitor, gates and grader. They are not measurements of any model. The baseline arm uses no model, so its rows are real measurements of that state machine.

live_pilot1.interpretation: First live pilot on the original held-out family, run before two harness fixes (idempotency-key reuse with a different payload was silently deduplicated; search scored raw token overlap). Its outcomes informed those fixes, so that family retired to development. Reported as measured.

live_pilot2.interpretation: Second live pilot on a fresh held-out family written and frozen after the fixes. Same model, prompts, caps and prices.

live_v2_mini.interpretation: v2 round on the fresh heldout3 family with the pre-registered search-before-reading rule (contract-prompts-v3). Same model, caps and prices as v1.

live_v2_sonnet.interpretation: v2 round, second model (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6) on the same heldout3 tasks: the guarded agent and the rule-based baseline, one run.

limitations: 30 synthetic tasks (10 dev, 10 retired held-out, 10 held-out) written by the author. A synthetic score does not certify that any agent is safe to deploy.
The deterministic baseline's rules were written for this suite's task phrasing; it is a reference point, not a general agent.
Executed violations are judged from simulated transitions. The harness has no real filesystem, network or approver, so it cannot show what a real side effect would cost.
Fixture rows for LLM arms are scripted and carry no information about model behaviour.
Each live pilot is one model, 10 held-out tasks and two runs at temperature 0: an exploratory sample. Run-to-run spread is shown as min and max.
